column3: The Greek explicitly says He knew “in Himself”; “teaching” specifies the demonstrative “this.”
“What will happen” supplies the unstated main clause of the Greek conditional question.
The Greek literally says they went “to the back,” expressed as “turned back.”
The Greek uses future “will we go,” rather than “would we go.”
The Greek uses perfect forms “have believed” and “have known,” rather than simple present.
The Greek connects the clauses with “and,” rather than “Yet.”
“Although” supplies a concessive link; the Greek identifies him as one of the Twelve without an explicit concessive word. BSB names Judas and Jesus for pronouns.
